source.title: How RL Reshapes LLM Reasoning: Transferability, Coverage, and Scaling Laws
source.authors: Ziheng Cheng; Yixiao Huang; Hanlin Zhu; Somayeh Sojoudi

record.tranche_reason: The study tests scaling behavior in RL compute and finds that log-sigmoid and log-linear fits can diverge during extrapolation, with saturation in some runs and predictive reliability varying by run and evaluation domain. It does not test the original pretraining-loss laws.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own RL-compute scaling fits. Its transfer, coverage and route-analysis results are not results about the claim's scaling laws. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. It fits log-sigmoid and log-linear curves of downstream benchmark accuracy against RL post-training compute (GPU-hours or optimizer steps) for one 14B model under two RL data mixtures. That is a related but different construct. V1–V4 and V7 concern pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or pretraining compute. V3 and V7 also concern compute-optimal N/D splits. V5 asks whether the same power-law loss form holds in other regimes, but this study fits accuracy, not loss, and its log-linear form is not a power law. V6 concerns downstream gains with model or pretraining scale or pretraining loss; RL steps on a fixed model are a different axis. The RL-compute findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that both laws approximate RL-compute score curves over a local compute range, and they give theoretical error bounds of O((b−a)^2) derived from strategy-selection dynamics. Which law extrapolates better varies by run: Math RL looks log-linear, while Math-Code RL saturates toward log-sigmoid. Benchmark predictability is weaker on coding and planning than on math, and longer-range forecasts need separate validation.
record.recipe_differences: Fits performance scores against RL compute (GPU hours or optimizer steps), rather than held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens or total pretraining compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Extrapolation varies with training mixture/run and evaluation domain; GPU-hour and optimizer-step fits yield similar qualitative conclusions. Log-sigmoid and log-linear curves are nearly indistinguishable over the fitting range but can diverge during extrapolation.

fits_no_version.finding: For Qwen3-14B GRPO runs fit through step 200, log-sigmoid and log-linear curves of benchmark accuracy versus RL compute fit about equally well. Fit R2 ranges from 0.83 to 0.99 per benchmark, and the authors say R2>0.99 for averages. Results are similar for GPU-hour and optimizer-step compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benchmark accuracy under RL post-training follows log-sigmoid or log-linear laws in RL compute over a local range.

fits_no_version.finding: When extrapolated to step 350 (about 2× fitting compute), Math RL tracks the log-linear prediction. Math-Code RL saturates: log-sigmoid tracks better and log-linear overpredicts. Coding and planning extrapolations are more brittle than math. This is stated qualitatively from Figures 5 and 9.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extrapolation of RL-compute scaling laws depends on the RL data mixture and the evaluation domain, and curves can bend toward saturation.

record.problems: Only two RL runs are fitted. The fitting range covers training through step 200, with extrapolation to step 350; coding and planning predictions are described as more brittle. Fit statistics are reported, but no uncertainty intervals for the scaling fits are stated. The log-sigmoid numerical optimization does not certify global optimality, and the Qwen3-Math-RL LiveCodeBench midpoint is weakly identified.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant scaling-fit result was omitted. The paper's empirical scaling section reports five individual benchmarks for two runs, with both GPU-hour and optimizer-step fits; these are all recorded.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
No power-law loss fits in other modalities or regimes. The RL fits are accuracy curves of log-sigmoid or log-linear form.
Downstream accuracy is not related to model scale or pretraining loss. A single 14B base model is used.
Pretraining exponents and N/D splits under different setups or fitting choices are not examined.

missing.what: Extrapolation accuracy (steps 200–350) for each law, run and benchmark. It is shown only graphically, with no error numbers, and no row records it. It matters only for a non-claim RL-scaling construct.
Fits to the five-benchmark average score (Figure 5f), with R2>0.99 on average.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked all rows to V7 and labelled V7 supports and limits_scope. V7 concerns pretraining-loss exponents and compute-optimal splits, so I removed those links and labels. The rows are fitted coefficients, not effect values, so 'partial' was not meaningful. The main focus of the paper (transfer, forgetting, Pass@N coverage) is unrelated to the claim. There is only one model size and two runs, with no uncertainty on the fits.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, tokens or training compute.
Whether pretraining-loss power laws fitted on small runs predict substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their growth with compute.
Architecture shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss; this study evaluates scores against RL compute instead.
Dependence of pretraining-loss exponents and compute-optimal parameter/token splits on setup; the study instead examines RL-compute score curves.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tested RL runs and evaluation benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: The fitted curve coefficients and fit quality vary by run and benchmark; the authors also report that the two curve forms diverge in extrapolation and that Math-Code RL saturates where log-linear fits overpredict (R01-R40).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Within the fitted range; tested RL-compute metrics and benchmark scores
reader_labels.reason: Both candidate laws fit the observed regime effectively, and the study's theoretical results justify them as local approximations; its evidence does not establish that pretraining-loss laws or compute-optimal splits have the same dependence (R01-R40).
